findings.reason: the remaining §7 node and the visible-lifetime surface have no owner in this repository, so the plan must point them at reckon's extension point and correct its artifact list, or a node rebuilds the duplicate the refactor removed.
findings.text: §6 declares "imas-ambix owns the node … Acquiring, holding, monitoring and releasing the allocation belongs here", and §7 step 3 (line 265) and step 6 (line 280) implement that here, but commit 6948258f (2026-09-28) removed imas_ambix/agent/fleet.py, the `agent fleet hold|place|status` commands, the four SiteConfig fleet_* settings and tests/agent/test_fleet.py, handing the owner to reckon (`reckon fleet-node hold|status|place`, reckon 15390017); both files are absent from the current tree while plan-artifacts (line 32) still lists imas_ambix/agent/fleet.py and tests/agent/test_fleet.py

findings.reason: the section must account for the added surface in its own text (naming what it retires, merges, or why nothing can be), and a sampler CLI that is invisible to `imas-ambix agent` is a surface decision the plan should make explicitly rather than leave to the module.
findings.text: §7.1 and the §7 steps add new interface families against a week whose cli_options and public_definitions both read 0: the throttling sampler ships its own argparse subcommand pair (sample/interval) with three options (--directory, --directory, --seconds) at imas_ambix/agent/throttling.py:533 and ~20 module-level public definitions, and steps 3/6 previously added the `agent fleet hold|status|place` CLI commands, while no section states what these retire, merge, or why nothing can be

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — imas_ambix/agent/throttling.py hides cgroup v2 parsing, ceiling-vs-no-ceiling and absent-vs-genuinely-zero semantics, host/boot identity, interval differencing and the JSON payload behind a small set of functions (read_sample, throttled_share, throttled_share_over_elapsed, interval_delta), so its 593 lines are hidden by roughly eight public entry points rather than spread across parallel wrappers.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — the plan assigns fleet-allocation holding and monitoring to imas-ambix, but that machinery was removed and re-homed to reckon, and the plan still names the deleted imas-ambix files as the artifacts that own it.
rubric_items.interface_budget: a finding — public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; the §7 implementation steps add CLI surface (`python -m imas_ambix.agent.throttling sample|interval`, three options) and public definitions in throttling.py, and previously `agent fleet hold|place|status`, without naming in their own text what they retire or merge, or why nothing can be.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — the plan ran a reuse map before proposing machinery (comment c-run-r-20260921T064359747219-fleet-reuse-map reports 103 resolved citations, establishing that sbatch generation/submission/registration/liveness already exist, that no cgroup cpu.stat reader exists anywhere in the checkout, and that reckon's reservation path exists but is unarmed); searches of the current tree corroborate it: throttling.py is the only cpu.stat reader (imas_ambix/agent/throttling.py, shared with imas_ambix/agent/telemetry_index.py), and the plan extended the existing squeue query in imas_ambix/agent/slurm.py rather than adding a second one.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — the one thin wrapper the plan added, `fleet place` over `srun --overlap --jobid`, carried an explicit justification for not extending reckon's reservation path (the second-allocation/one-node-whole conflict at comment c-20260922-placement-resolves-by-token), so it is a wrapper with the required reason rather than a finding.
